summary: I sent the prompt word for word. The context was auto-compacted twice while the agent read the notes: once after 04-market.txt and once after 06-lighthouse.txt. After each compaction the agent went on to the next unread file. It never called the Skill tool and never re-read a file it had already read. It named notes/06-lighthouse.txt, quoted the relit-lamp sentence exactly, and gave a one-line summary of each of the eight files. The repo is unchanged.
reasoning: All three acceptance criteria are met, and the session log confirms them. The agent did not start reading skills after compaction: the log has no Skill tool call. It finished in about 59 seconds without asking any questions, so I never had to give one of the scripted replies.

observations.description: Compaction behaviour in the session log: there are two system compact_boundary events, at 19:08:42 and 19:09:05. Tool calls after the first one: Read 05-railway, then 06-lighthouse. After the second: Read 07-vineyard, then 08-orchard. There was no Skill tool_use anywhere and no file was re-read. The scenario's core intent held.

After the compactions the transcript showed 'Referenced file 02-quarry.txt' and 'Referenced file 01-harbor.txt' twice each, plus 06-lighthouse and 05-railway. The duplicate entries look a little noisy.

On launch, Claude Code showed a 'Newer Opus model available — Currently pinned: Opus 5, Latest: Opus 5.5' dialog, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No. The banner then showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI', so the dialog seems unnecessary or contradictory when the model is already given on the command line.
The workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit'. That is safe, but it is easy to quit by accident when you press Enter.

The agent stated that 'every other line in every file is random word salad'. That fits the fixture, and the summaries also pointed out paragraphs repeated across files (market/glacier, orchard/vineyard).

criteria.criterion: Names notes/06-lighthouse.txt and quotes the relit-lamp sentence
criteria.evidence: Screen: "The passage is in notes/06-lighthouse.txt, at line 227 ... \"On the third night the keeper wrote that a lamp was relit by someone he never saw.\"" Running grep -n relit notes/* returned the same line: notes/06-lighthouse.txt:227.

criteria.criterion: Gives a one-line summary for each of the eight files
criteria.evidence: Screen shows a numbered list from 1. 01-harbor.txt to 8. 08-orchard.txt, one line each, e.g. "6. 06-lighthouse.txt: Random lighthouse-themed notes about lamps, the keeper, storms and the tide, plus the one real sentence..."

criteria.criterion: Does not modify any file in the repository
criteria.evidence: After the run, `git status --short --untracked-files=all` in coding-agent-workdir printed nothing (rc=0). The session log has only Bash (ls/wc) and Read tool calls, with no Edit or Write.
